unnamed_1: Keywords are indicators of things that "happened" on each leg of the race. These include common types of challenges and phenomenon that occur during multiple different seasons of TAR.

unnamed_2: Legs include:
challenge(s) that involve riding, herding, and/or working with animals in some way, such as riding an elephant or towing a field with an ox.
challenge(s) that involve some level of attention to detail, such as setting a dinner table or locating a specific tile.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to balance in some way.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to ride any type of bicycle to move around.
challenge(s) that require the assembly of something - provided instructions or otherwise.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to cook something to the acceptance of judges, like cooking fish over a fire, but not necessarily consume it.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to count specific things, like beans placed in urns.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to learn choreographed moves to perform for judges, may include routines other than dancing such as color guard or martial arts.
team member(s) driving some kind of automobile to move around, most commonly driving a car to the next clue, almost always includes navigating.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to identify international/domestic flags.
challenge(s) where team member(s) are required to consume food and/or drinks, not applicable for teams voluntarily consuming food and/or drinks.
team member(s) using and/or indentifying geography for a challenge or to get to the next destination.
challenge(s) that utilize the hand eye coordination of team member(s), in tasks like baseball and soccer.
challenge(s) that take place at large heights that tap into team member(s) fear, such as skydiving and bungee jumping.
clue(s) and/or challenge(s) that include a foreign language that needs to be translated and/or memorized to complete the task or travel to the next destination.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to use mathematics to complete it, like adding up money or various books.

challenge(s) that require team member(s) to memorize part of the task to complete it OR challenge(s) at the end of the race requiring team member(s) to remember things like challenges and route markers to complete the task.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to learn to play a piece on a musical instrument or read and/or memorize sheet music.
challenge(s) that specifically involve teams using a given map to complete it, it's worth noting that every legs requires teams to navigate from clue to clue.
challenge(s) that make team member(s) go through pain to complete the task, such as an intense massage and swimming in freezing cold water.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to paint something to complete it with specific attention to detail, such as painting a colorful door.
challenge(s) or moment(s) that require team member(s) to utilze physical strength to complete, such as running to clues and moving massive hay bales.
clue(s) and/or challenge(s) that require team member(s) to solve a puzzle of some sort to move on, such as riddles, rebus puzzles, slide puzzles, etc.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to search for something to complete the task, such as a route marker, or find the next destination.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to rely on non-players to donate funds to meet a quota while they beg and/or perform.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to learn a song to sing and perform for judges.
challenge(s) that require team member(s) to swim in a body of water to receive the next clue and/or complete the leg.
team(s) running into any kind of issues traveling during the leg, such as flight delays, car troubles, getting lost, etc.
*NOTE: many challenges fufill multiple keywords, hopefully in the future I can lay out what keywords apply to each challenge throughout TAR
